Script:


Fees Must Fall – Update

VO: The last two weeks have seen thousands of university students protesting and demanding a zero percent fees increase for 2016, free education for all and an end to outsourcing of key university services.

VO: By the end of the week Dr Max Price, the Vice Chancellor of the University of Cape Town agreed to end this practice.

UPSOUND Max Price: We decided that we will commit to insourcing. We’ve signed an agreement with Nehawu...which is the union which represents most of the workers in the outsourced companies at UCT.

VO: This marked yet another victory for students whose 9-day nationwide protests brought the country’s public universities to a standstill and forced government to intervene.

UPSOUND President Jacob Zuma: “We agreed that there will be a zero percent increase of University fees in 2016.”

VO: But despite this victory, protests continued calling for all demands to be met.

UPSOUND Phindile Maphangwa: We wanted free education in the long term ...and the institution of higher learning needs to be transformed.

VO: This week in the Eastern Cape, violence flared at Fort Hare and Nelson Mandela Metropolitan Universities.

VO: On Monday the University of Cape Town closed for the week and announced that charges against 23 students had been withdrawn.

VO: At Wits University, doors reopened on Wednesday, but classes were again disrupted as small groups of protesters demanded an end to outsourcing.

UPSOUND Nomhle Mcomge: We promised that we would sort out the issue of outsourcing and also that we would not stop until education was made free for all.

VO: With the Presidential Task Team investigating issues relating to Higher Education, calm returned to most universities as classes resumed.

SOUND UP Phindile: The revolution needs to be advanced in a way that won’t compromise the same working class that we are advocating for.
